# SchemaShield

SchemaShield is a synchronous JSON Schema interpreter for Node.js, Bun, and compatible serverless or edge runtimes. It supports draft-04, draft-06, draft-07, 2019-09, and 2020-12 through one API.

Near-zero validator overhead at cold start, with no runtime source-code generation.

README.md is the canonical adoption guide. REFERENCE.md contains exhaustive API and compatibility contracts.

## Verified properties

- No runtime source-code generation. The library does not call `eval()` or `new Function()`.
- No implicit network, file, or DNS access during compilation or validation.
- Zero runtime dependencies.
- Nineteen built-in official metaschema resources.
- Compile-time metavalidation of every reachable resource by default.
- Synchronous validators reusable within one process or isolate.
- JSON data and live JavaScript object validation.
- Custom types, formats, keywords, metaschemas, and local schema resources.
- Configurable recursive validation depth.
- String-length keywords count Unicode code points.
- High sustained validation throughput and near-zero validator overhead at cold start.

Measured execution uses reusable validators for sustained throughput. Cold execution creates a fresh context, performs validator construction, configuration, registrations and setup when required, and runs the first validation. It excludes runtime process startup and module import, so the cold-start claim covers validator overhead only. Every measured case must produce its expected result before timing is accepted. Measure application-specific schemas on the target runtime for capacity planning.

## Install

```bash
npm install schema-shield
```

```javascript
import { SchemaShield } from "schema-shield";
```

Node.js package entry points require Node.js 18 or later. CommonJS and TypeScript declarations are included. There is no default export.

## Basic use

```javascript
const validateUser = new SchemaShield().compile({
  type: "object",
  properties: {
    name: { type: "string", minLength: 1 },
    email: { type: "string", format: "email" }
  },
  required: ["name", "email"],
  additionalProperties: false
});

validateUser({ name: "John", email: "john@example.com" });
// { data: { name: "John", email: "john@example.com" }, error: null, valid: true }

validateUser({ email: "invalid" });
// { data: { email: "invalid" }, error: true, valid: false }
```

The result shape is always `{ data, error, valid }`.

## Error modes

`failFast` defaults to `true`. Normal data failures return `error: true` in this mode. Set `failFast: false` before accessing `ValidationError` methods.

```javascript
const validate = new SchemaShield({ failFast: false }).compile({
  type: "object",
  properties: {
    age: { type: "integer", minimum: 18 }
  },
  required: ["age"]
});

const result = validate({ age: 16 });

if (!result.valid && result.error !== true) {
  result.error.getPath();
  result.error.getCause();
  result.error.getTree();
}
```

Both modes stop at the first failing path. `getTree()` returns the causal chain for that failure. It does not collect independent failures across the input.

## Configuration

```typescript
new SchemaShield({
  immutable?: boolean;
  failFast?: boolean;
  format?: boolean;
  maxDepth?: number;
  useDefaults?: boolean | "empty";
})
```

- `immutable: true` validates a `structuredClone` of the root value.
- `failFast: false` enables detailed causal errors.
- `format: true` validates every registered format across dialects.
- `format: false` disables optional format assertions.
- `maxDepth` defaults to `128` and accepts integers from `1` through `256`.
- `useDefaults: true` fills absent or `undefined` properties.
- `useDefaults: "empty"` also replaces `null` and `""`.

Defaults mutate the validated value. Invalid inserted defaults can remain after failure. Immutable mode inherits `structuredClone` behavior. Class instances lose their prototype, and unsupported values such as functions, promises, weak collections, and symbols make cloning throw.

## Compile once per process or isolate

Compile at module scope or during startup, then reuse the validator across requests in that process or isolate.

```javascript
const validateRequest = new SchemaShield().compile(requestSchema);

app.post("/users", (request, response) => {
  const result = validateRequest(request.body);

  if (!result.valid) {
    return response.status(400).json({ error: "Invalid request" });
  }

  return response.status(201).json(result.data);
});
```

Do not claim that one compiled function is automatically shared across worker threads, processes, or isolates.

## Compatible Worker pattern

This Cloudflare Workers pattern applies to a runtime that supports the package's JavaScript requirements. It is an integration recipe, rather than a general platform certification.

```javascript
import { SchemaShield } from "schema-shield";

const validateRequest = new SchemaShield({ failFast: false }).compile({
  type: "object",
  properties: {
    name: { type: "string", minLength: 1 },
    email: { type: "string", format: "email" }
  },
  required: ["name", "email"],
  additionalProperties: false
});

export default {
  async fetch(request) {
    let data;

    try {
      data = await request.json();
    } catch {
      return Response.json({ error: "Invalid JSON" }, { status: 400 });
    }

    const result = validateRequest(data);

    if (!result.valid) {
      return Response.json(
        { error: result.error.getPath() },
        { status: 400 }
      );
    }

    return Response.json(result.data);
  }
};
```

Parse request streams before validation.

## Drafts and format policy

Declare `$schema` when behavior depends on an official dialect. `compile()` metavalidates the complete reachable graph by default. Use `{ validateSchema: false }` only when the application already validated that complete graph.

- With `format: true`, registered formats validate in every dialect.
- With `format: false`, optional format assertions are disabled.
- With the option omitted, schemas without `$schema` validate formats.
- Official dialects treat formats as annotations when the option is omitted.
- A custom dialect requiring `format-assertion` validates known formats and rejects unknown formats.

## Local resources and references

HTTP and HTTPS URIs identify local resources. They never trigger retrieval.

```javascript
const shield = new SchemaShield();

shield.addSchema(addressSchema, {
  uri: "https://schemas.example/address"
});

const validate = shield.compile({
  type: "object",
  properties: {
    address: { $ref: "https://schemas.example/address" }
  }
});
```

Register every reachable resource before compilation. Registration stores a snapshot, rejects duplicate identities, and affects future compilations.

## Extensions

```javascript
const shield = new SchemaShield({ failFast: false });

shield.addType("safe-integer", Number.isSafeInteger);

shield.addFormat("ticket-id", (value) =>
  /^TKT-[0-9]{6}$/.test(value)
);

shield.addKeyword("divisibleBy", (schema, data, defineError) => {
  if (typeof data === "number" && data % schema.divisibleBy !== 0) {
    return defineError("Value is not divisible", {
      code: "NOT_DIVISIBLE",
      data
    });
  }
});
```

Existing active extension names require `overwrite: true`. Custom functions are synchronous and belong to the application's trust boundary.

## Integration limits

- Recursive validation uses `maxDepth`, with default `128` and range `1` through `256`.
- Compilation has a separate fixed graph-depth limit of `128`.
- The root schema `{}` is currently rejected. Use `true` for an always-valid root.
- Data-validation failures return results. Compilation, clone, custom-code, and programming failures can throw.
- The current fail-fast unknown-type compilation edge can throw the literal `true`.
- Schema URI schemes never enable network access.
- Resources are local, additive, snapshot-based, and per instance.
